title: Rank, alpha, DoRA, LoKr and the other adapters

questions.q: What can a LoKr change reach that a rank 4 LoRA change can't, from far fewer numbers?
options: Full rank, since a Kronecker product's rank is the product of its factors' ranks
questions.answer: Full rank, since a Kronecker product's rank is the product of its factors' ranks
questions.why: The lab measures rank 96 from 208 numbers. But it's one shape repeated, so it fits a low-rank target poorly.

questions.q: In TrainLoraNode with algorithm LoKr and rank 8, what does the 8 mean?
options: A factor for splitting the layer's size: 1280 becomes 8 and 160
questions.answer: A factor for splitting the layer's size: 1280 becomes 8 and 160
questions.why: create_train calls factorization(out_dim, rank). Plain w1 and w2 come out of it, with no rank at all.

questions.q: A LoKr file has plain lokr_w1 and lokr_w2 and an alpha of 1. What does alpha do?
options: Nothing: scale is 1.0 without a decomposed factor
questions.answer: Nothing: scale is 1.0 without a decomposed factor
questions.why: calculate_weight only uses alpha if dim was set, which only happens when a factor was decomposed.

questions.q: What does a dora_scale key do to a layer at strength 1, in the column form?
options: Rescales each column to the stored size after adding the change
questions.answer: Rescales each column to the stored size after adding the change
questions.why: weight_decompose divides by the new column norm and multiplies by dora_scale. The lab's sizes come out at the stored value.

questions.q: Why does comfy offer a bypass path for quantized models?
options: The change is computed beside the layer, so it needn't survive rounding into the stored format
questions.answer: The change is computed beside the layer, so it needn't survive rounding into the stored format
questions.why: h(x) is added to the output. Merging into 8 bits can lose a small change, as CU-212 measures.
